question: Where the right-click lock of the production and technology sliders is kept, what sets and clears it, whether it reaches the savegame or a command, whether the balancing reads it there, and whether the screens are built once per session.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_ToggleLock
addresses.comment: **The right-click lock of a scrollbar.** Nothing unless the scrollbar is `lockable` (+0x250, the .gui key). Reads its slider button's state (+0xA0, slot 44): 4 (being dragged) - nothing; 3 (disabled) and +0x253 clear - SetState(0) (slot 45), unlocked; otherwise SetState(3), locked - which includes a slider already disabled while +0x253 says code disabled it, so a right click never unlocks a scrollbar code switched off. Two references, both in CScrollbar_Construct's observer for the slider button (+0xF8): the glue's slot 8 (handler +0x30, run by GuiSliderButton_HandleMouse on input sub-kind 5, likely the double click) directly, and slot 9, the right click, through CScrollbar_OnSliderRightClick. **The lock is only the button's state**: nothing here writes the scrollbar, the view or a country. Bare `ret`. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xA9FF60..0xA9FFC6: cmp byte [esi+0x250],0; [[esi+0xA0]]+0xB0 (slot 44) compared with 4 and 3; cmp byte [esi+0x253],0; [[esi+0xA0]]+0xB4 (slot 45) with push 0 or push 3; bare ret at 0xA9FFB2 and 0xA9FFC6. Slot 44 of the button tables is 0x8AF4D0 (mov eax,[ecx+0x64]) and slot 45 is 0xACFF80 (mov [ecx+0x64],arg). Only references: the immediate at 0xA9DC0E (11th argument of CButtonObserver_Init for +0xF8, stored at +0x30, read by the glue's slot 8 0x6B6DE0) and the call from 0xA9FFD0. Wrong if CButtonObserver_Init's argument k did not land at +8+4(k-1) - read at 0xA9A743..0xA9A7B5.

addresses.name: CScrollbar_OnSliderRightClick
addresses.comment: The slider button's right click: `call CScrollbar_ToggleLock; ret 4`, the button the listener is handed left unread. Stored by CScrollbar_Construct as the 15th argument of the +0xF8 observer, so at its +0x40, which the observer glue's slot 9 (0x6C35C0, `ret 4`) calls - slot 9 being what a button runs on the right button's up after its down. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xA9FFD0..0xA9FFD5: e8 -> 0xA9FF60, c2 04 00. Its one reference is the immediate at 0xA9DC03 (pushed as the observer's 15th argument). Slot 9 of vftable 0x15FF6DC is 0x6C35C0, which jumps to [glue+0x40] with ECX = [glue+0x44] + [glue+4] and returns ret 4. That slot 9 is the right click: GuiSliderButton_HandleMouse and GuiButton_HandleMouse both reach it through 0xACFF60 only on event +0x10 == 4 with +0x14 == 2 after +0x70 was set by +0x10 == 3, +0x14 == 2. Wrong if +0x14 == 2 were not the right button (the left is +0x14 == 1, the press arm).

addresses.name: GuiSliderButton_HandleMouse
addresses.signature: void __fastcall GuiSliderButton_HandleMouse(void* button@ECX, void* event@stack:4, void* input@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **Slot 1 of GuiObject_sliderButton (0x15FFB38), the scrollbar knob's mouse handler**; `ret 8`. For an event of kind 0 (event +8) on a shown (+0x2C) knob that takes the mouse (+0x84): sub-kind 5 (event +0x10, likely the double click) runs the listeners' slots 8 and 7 and marks the event handled; sub-kind 3 with button 2 (+0x14) sets +0x70; sub-kind 4 with button 2 over a set +0x70 clears it and runs the listeners' slot 9 (0xACFF60) - **the right click, before and regardless of the button's state**, so a disabled knob (state 3) still takes it. Only then does it test the state: a left press (3 with button 1) on a knob not in state 3 or 4 sets state 4 and runs slot 4; a left release with state 1 or 4 sets 2 and runs slot 2; in state 3 neither. GuiButton_HandleMouse, the ordinary button's, drops every event on a state-3 button, which is why a locked slider can be unlocked only because its knob is this class. The second argument is an input object asked slots 11, 12 and 13 (+0x2C, +0x30, +0x34). Not read past the left-button arms. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Held at slot 1 of the table 0x15FFB38 (the dword at 0x15FFB3C), its only reference. Decoded 0xAA14C0..0xAA165D: cmp [ebx+8],0; cmp [edi+0x2c],0; cmp [edi+0x84],0; eax=[ebx+0x10]: ==5 -> 0xACFF20, 0xACFF40 (slots 8 and 7: [vtbl+0x20], [vtbl+0x1C]); ==3 && [ebx+0x14]==2 -> [edi+0x70]=1; ==4 && [ebx+0x14]==2 && [edi+0x70]==1 -> [edi+0x70]=0, call 0xACFF60 ([vtbl+0x24], slot 9) at 0xAA155B; the first test of [edi+0x64] against 3 is at 0xAA157A, after all of that. Positive control: GuiButton_HandleMouse 0xACFBE0 tests [edi+0x64]==3 at 0xACFC0C before any arm and takes 0xACFD72, which runs no listener.

addresses.name: GuiSliderButton_Construct
addresses.no_signature: the type in EDX, the memory at [ebp+8] and six more stack arguments not identified one by one; ret 0x1C
addresses.comment: **The constructor of GuiObject_sliderButton, a scrollbar's knob.** Calls the button base (0xACFA70) and writes vftable 0x15FFB38 at +0 and 0x15FFC54 at +0x48 (0xAA1018, 0xAA101E); 0xB8 bytes. One caller, GuiSliderButton_Create. So the knob a scrollbar makes from its `slider` declaration is this class and not the ordinary guiButtonType widget (0x1607698). The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md, section 6.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xAA0FE0..0xAA1040 and the ret 0x1C at 0xAA126C. findValue(0x15FFB38) in .text gives 0xAA101A and 0xAA12C2 only; the second is the next function (0xAA12A0, functionStart, likely the destructor). findRefs --callers 0xAA0FE0: one, 0xB2C48D. Wrong if 0xAA12A0 were the constructor - it starts after int3 padding and the store at 0xAA12C2 follows no allocation.

addresses.name: GuiSliderButton_Create
addresses.no_signature: the guiButtonType type in ESI, five stack arguments (ret 0x14) of which [ebp+8], [ebp+0xC] and [ebp+0x10] are passed on; returns the button in EAX
addresses.comment: Allocates 0xB8 bytes and constructs a GuiObject_sliderButton (GuiSliderButton_Construct) from the guiButtonType in ESI, passing its +0x104, +0x120 and the words at +0x254/+0x258. Three callers: 0xB29514, the lookup CScrollbar_Construct uses for its `slider` (0xB29450, which finds the guiButtonType child of that name and makes it with this, then adds it to the parent through +0x15C's slot 16), 0xA7CC1A and 0xAC726B - the eight knobs beyond the 92 scrollbars FINDINGS-guilive.md counted. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xB2C420..0xB2C49F: push 0xB8; call 0xB9602F (operator new); the stores from [esi+0x254]/[esi+0x258]; lea [esi+0x120], lea [esi+0x104]; mov edx,esi; call 0xAA0FE0; ret 0x14 at 0xB2C49F. findRefs --callers: 0xA7CC1A, 0xAC726B, 0xB29514. CScrollbar_Construct reaches it through call 0xB29450 at 0xA9DFE1 and stores the result at +0xA0 (0xA9DFE6). `inferred` only for the two other callers, not read.

addresses.name: GuiType_scrollbarType_LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __fastcall GuiType_scrollbarType_LoadKey(void* type@ECX, CParseContext* parse@stack:4, SaveToken key@stack:8)
addresses.comment: **The `scrollbarType` grammar of a .gui file**, slot 4 of GuiType_scrollbarType (0x1606958). Read only for two keys: token 0x144 `lockable` into the type's byte +0x198 and token 0x145 `drag` into +0x199, each through the yes/no reader 0xA7B410; the type's constructor sets both bytes as the word 0x100 (0xB282E6), so `lockable` defaults to no and `drag` to yes. The scrollbar's create (0xB284C0) hands both, with the word +0x184, to CScrollbar_Construct, which keeps them at the live scrollbar's +0x250 and +0x251. The rest of the grammar was not read; switchmap.py names 22 of its cases (size, position, borderSize, parent, leftButton, rightButton, slider, track, priority, minValue, maxValue, stepSize, startValue, horizontal and the child types). `ret 8`. The name is ours.
addresses.evidence: Held at slot 4 of the table 0x1606958 (the dword at 0x1606968). Decoded 0xB28C30..0xB28C5B: cmp eax,0x144; je 0xB28F14, which does add esi,0x198; push esi; call 0xA7B410; ret 8. The second jump table (0xB2910C, byte table 0xB29128, base token 0x145) sends 0x145 to 0xB28F53: add esi,0x199; call 0xA7B410. ghidra/saveTokens.json gives 324 = lockable and 325 = drag; the registration of 0x144 against the string 'lockable' is at 0xCF86B5..0xCF86C7. Wrong if 0xA7B410 were not a boolean reader (the bytes it fills are read as bytes, 0xB284FB/0xB28502).

addresses.name: CProductionView::BuildSliders
addresses.comment: **Makes the six IC sliders.** Clears the list at +0xB8, then for each of the country's ProductionDistribution (+0x5F4..+0x5F8), in index order, allocates 0x40 bytes and constructs a CEconomySlider on the window 'domesticpanel_slider', and **puts it at the front of the list** - so the list runs upgrade, reinforcement, supply, production, consumer goods, lend-lease, the order of the six icons down the .gui file. The country is the played one (the in-game screen's slot 23 at +0xB0, its id into the country database). **The lock comes back from the country here**: the distribution at index i is matched with slider_locks (+0x1090) entry count - 1 - i, which is its place in the list, and where that entry is inside the vector and above 0 the slider's knob (scrollbar `actual_slider`'s +0xA0) is disabled through its slot 47 - locked. Called from CProductionView::AttachButtons (so the constructor and slot 0) and from CProductionView::Update when the played country changes. `ret 4`. The name is ours.
addresses.revises: comment: the index rule (count - 1 - i, the list place), the knob's slot 47, which country, and the two callers
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x7FC48C..0x7FC6E9: the country from [[0x1A855A4]+0x16C][id] with the id from [esi+0xB0]'s slot 23 ([edx+0x5c]); [esp+0x14] = (+0x5F8 - +0x5F4)/4 - 1 at 0x7FC4B3, decremented at 0x7FC6CD each pass; at 0x7FC557..0x7FC580 the bound test against (+0x1094 - +0x1090)/4 and >= 0, then cmp [ecx+eax*4],0; setg; then 'actual_slider' found through the window's slot 19 ([edx+0x4c]) and [[eax+0xA0]]+0xBC called (slot 47, 0xACFFA0: [ecx+0x64] = 3). findRefs --callers 0x7FC350: 0x7FC337 (AttachButtons) and 0x7FD449 (Update). What changed: the index rule and the callers; the old sentence is kept in substance.

addresses.name: CTechnologyView::Build
addresses.comment: **Makes the four leadership sliders and wires the folder buttons.** Clears the list at +0xBC, then for each of the country's LeadershipDistribution (+0x5E4..+0x5E8), in index order, constructs a CEconomySlider on the window 'tech_slider' with the IC flag clear and **puts it at the front of the list** - so the list runs research, espionage, diplomacy, officers, the order of the four icons - adding its window to the one at +0x184. **It locks a slider from the country's slider_locks (+0x1090) - the production screen's vector**: leadership distribution i is matched with entry 3 - i (its list place) and its knob disabled (slot 47) where that entry is above 0. Nothing on the technology screen writes the vector, so research, espionage, diplomacy and officers come up locked where upgrade, reinforcement, supply and production were last locked on the production screen (or in the save loaded), and a lock set on the technology screen is never kept. Then, for every technology folder from index 1, the button 'techtree_' + folder key is given the view's observer, and the first folder with a button becomes the selected one at +0x15C. Also attaches to `start` and `close` of `tech_details`. Called from the constructor and from slot 0 (0x81D0D0). `ret 4`. The name is ours.
addresses.revises: comment: adds that it reads the production screen's slider_locks for its four sliders, by list place, and its two callers
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x81A560..0x81A6BA and 0x81A7BD: [esp+0x20] = (+0x5E8 - +0x5E4)/4 - 1 at 0x81A586, decremented at 0x81A7BD; at 0x81A649..0x81A66E the same bound test and cmp [ecx+eax*4],0; setg as BuildSliders; 'actual_slider', [[eax+0xA0]]+0xBC. The universe of +0x1090/+0x1094/+0x1098 in .text (a sweep of 2,755,661 instructions decoded chunk by chunk with resumes, reaching the section's end) is: CCountry::CCountry, its unwind funclets, the destructor 0x4CA740, CCountry::LoadKey, CCountry::SaveContents, CCountry_Reset, CProductionView::BuildSliders, CProductionView_Update_BalanceSliders, and this - nothing in CTechnologyView's update (0x81B0C0) or anywhere else. Positive control: the same sweep finds +0x108C's known writer CCountry::RecountUnitTotals (0x4E2323) and the three inc sites, and +0x1090's two known production readers. findRefs --callers 0x81A510: 0x81A492 (constructor), 0x81D122 (slot 0 of CTechnologyView).

addresses.name: CEconomySlider::OnNeedButton
addresses.comment: **What `ic_need_button` does.** If the setting's slot 7 says it has a window of its own - only lend-lease's does - calls its slot 8 and returns. Otherwise sets the slider to need + half a step, the need being the setting's slot 3 and the step the scrollbar's +0x234 over a thousand; then disables the slider's own button and sets +0x3E, pinning it to its need - unless the button was already disabled (its slot 44 answering 3), in which case it is enabled again if the scrollbar's +0x253 is set. **Nothing sets +0x253 on a production or technology slider** (its only writers are CSettingsScreen_Refresh, CObjectivesEntry::Update and the unnamed virtual 0x42E1D0, held at 0x15B6478), so on these screens the need button always moves the slider to its need and leaves it locked, whether or not it was locked before - it never unlocks. The value is set before the state is looked at. The name is ours.
addresses.revises: comment: adds that +0x253 is never set on these sliders, so the need button always ends locked
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x7F0080..0x7F0288: SetValue (0x7F0CC0) at 0x7F013C before the slot 44 test at 0x7F018F; locked arm 0x7F01EB cmp byte [esi+0x253],0, slot 46 ([edx+0xB8]) only when set, then the byte cleared; unlocked arm slot 47 ([edx+0xBC]) and byte [esi+0x3E] = 1. The writers of byte [reg+0x253] = 1 in the whole of .text (the same chunked sweep) are 0x42E1DA, 0x6FA371, 0x6FA390, 0x6FA3AF and 0x74F793 - none in CProductionView, CTechnologyView or CEconomySlider. Wrong if a scrollbar's +0x253 were set through a pointer to it (a `lea reg,[x+0x253]` - the sweep found none).

addresses.name: CCountry_Reset
addresses.comment: A long reset of a country's state - frees and empties several lists (+0xBAC, +0xBBC, +0x119C ...), zeroes the `tech_decay_modifier` vector (+0x1174) for every technology category, and sets **neutrality (+0xA8C) to g_CountryDefaultNeutrality, 50.000** (0x4D307F). Called from the tail of CCountry::CCountry (0x4CA64E) and from ResetSession_ClearLoadedFromSave (0x67BDFC) over the country vector. 0x4D2B60 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D4B88, 10 int3 above. Only the stretch 0x4D2F80-0x4D30D0 was read; the name is from its shape and its two callers. **Espionage** (read 2026-10-14, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-espionage.md section A; esi is the function's zero, `xor esi, esi` at 0x4D2B84 and again at 0x4D4396): spy_pool (+0x1170) = 0 (0x4D2EBA) and spiescaught (+0x11D4) = 0 (0x4D2BA7); every presence through CSpyPresence::Reset (0x4D48C0); then the country's own presence, when its id is inside the vector, gets priority 1 and SetMissionAllocation(counter-espionage, 1) (0x4D4927-0x4D493D) - the same as InitCountryPerCountryArrays' tail. Called from CCountry::CCountry before the vector exists (so that part does nothing there) and over every country on a session reset. **The IC shares and the slider locks** (read 2026-11-13, reversing/findings/FINDINGS-countryviews.md section 6; 0x4D471D-0x4D47B1): every ProductionDistribution's base_percentage (+8) is set to 2^30 / (count << 15) - an equal share in fixed 15 - with the setting's slot 4 called where that changed it, and slider_locks (+0x1090) entry i set to 0 for each, written in place without a bound test.
addresses.revises: comment: appends the IC shares' reset and the zeroing of slider_locks
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0x4D471D..0x4D47B1: push (count<<15) as a 64-bit divisor, push esi (0), push 0x40000000, call 0xB99980; the loop over +0x5F4[i] stores the quotient at the setting's +8/+0xC, compares with the old and calls [vtbl+0x10] when it differs; at 0x4D4796 mov ecx,[ebx+0x1090]; mov [ecx+edi*4],esi. ESI is zeroed at 0x4D4396 and is callee-saved across every call between there and 0x4D4796 (no write to ESI in that stretch). Everything before the appended sentence is the record's comment unchanged.

struct_fields.name: slider_button
struct_fields.comment: The knob: the GuiObject_sliderButton (vftable 0x15FFB38) CScrollbar_Construct makes from the guiButtonType its `slider` key names (0xA9DFE6). Its state (+0x64; slot 44 reads it, 45 sets it, 46 enables, 47 disables) is 3 when disabled - **which is the lock** of a production or technology slider, set by CScrollbar_ToggleLock, CEconomySlider::OnNeedButton and the two views' slider builders, and tested by CEconomySlider::IsDisabled. The end buttons test it too: neither moves the bar while it is 3.
struct_fields.evidence: Store at 0xA9DFE6 from call 0xB29450; read at 0xA9E3D4 (observer +0xF8 attached to it), 0xA9FF6C (ToggleLock), 0x7F0187 and 0x7FC5BC (via 'actual_slider'). Wrong if CEconomySlider's 'actual_slider' lookup did not answer this scrollbar (it is the window's scrollbar of that name, FINDINGS-countryviews.md section 2).

struct_fields.name: lockable
struct_fields.comment: The .gui key `lockable` (the type's +0x198, token 0x144), copied by CScrollbar_Construct (0xA9DDC4). CScrollbar_ToggleLock does nothing without it. `lockable = yes` is on actual_slider in country_production.gui and country_technology.gui, on lendlease.gui's slider and on orders.gui's; the type defaults it to no.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA9DDAA mov cl,[ebp+0x64]; 0xA9DDC4 mov [ebx+0x250],cl - the argument the create 0xB284C0 pushes from movzx [esi+0x198] (0xB28502); GuiType_scrollbarType_LoadKey writes +0x198 on token 0x144. Only reader: 0xA9FF63.

struct_fields.name: drag
struct_fields.comment: The .gui key `drag` (the type's +0x199, token 0x145, default yes), copied by CScrollbar_Construct (0xA9DDBE). Where it is set the constructor attaches the knob's observer (+0xF8: press, release, the double-click and right-click toggle) to the knob and the track's to the track (0xA9E3CB); where it is not, the knob takes neither a drag nor the lock.
struct_fields.evidence: 0xA9DDB4 mov dl,[ebp+0x68]; 0xA9DDBE mov [ebx+0x251],dl, from movzx [esi+0x199] at 0xB284FB; LoadKey writes +0x199 on token 0x145, which saveTokens.json gives as `drag`. Read at 0xA9E3CB, je past both observer attachments.

struct_fields.name: disabled_by_code
struct_fields.comment: Set to 1 by code that switches a scrollbar off itself (CSettingsScreen_Refresh, CObjectivesEntry::Update, the unnamed virtual 0x42E1D0) before disabling its knob. While it is set a right click cannot unlock the knob (CScrollbar_ToggleLock locks it again), and CEconomySlider::OnNeedButton, CEconomySlider::ResetFromSetting, 0xA9E680 and 0x42E180 enable the knob again and clear it. Nothing sets it on a production or technology slider. The name is ours.
struct_fields.evidence: Writers of byte [reg+0x253] in .text: 1 at 0x42E1DA, 0x6FA371, 0x6FA390, 0x6FA3AF, 0x74F793; 0 at 0x42E1A4, 0x7F0050, 0x7F0203, 0xA9E699. Readers: 0x42E18B, 0x7F0038, 0x7F01EB, 0xA9E680, 0xA9FF96. Each reader that finds it set calls the knob's slot 46 (enable). Wrong if the five setters were on another class with a byte at +0x253 - each is followed by a call through that object's +0xA0, the knob.

struct_fields.name: slider_locks
struct_fields.comment: **The production screen's slider locks**, a vector of ints (end +0x1094, capacity +0x1098), one per ProductionDistribution, made by CCountry::CCountry with that many zeros. Indexed by the slider's place in the screen's list - 0 upgrade, 1 reinforcement, 2 supply, 3 production, 4 consumer goods, 5 lend-lease - 1 for locked. **A mirror of the knobs, not the lock itself**: CProductionView_Update_BalanceSliders writes each entry from CEconomySlider::IsDisabled every round of every frame the production screen is open, and CProductionView::BuildSliders disables a knob whose entry is above 0 when it makes the sliders. CTechnologyView::Build reads entries 0 to 3 for its own four sliders (research, espionage, diplomacy, officers) and nothing on that screen writes them. CCountry_Reset zeroes every entry; CCountry::LoadKey clears the vector and reads `slider_locks` (token 0x696) into it; CCountry::SaveContents writes it only for the country the local player plays (the in-game screen's slot 23 against +0xCA8), so a save holds one `slider_locks` block, in the player's country - 60 of the maintainer's saves have exactly one, `0 0 0 0 0 0`, and one (an olderautosave.hoi3 of 2026-11-12, likely written by OpenHOI3) none. Nothing else reads it: no Lua accessor, no command, no AI code. Renamed from distribution_locked, which no consumer used, to the game's own key.
struct_fields.revises: name distribution_locked -> slider_locks (the save key); comment rewritten: the index by list place, the mirror, the technology screen's read, the reset, load and save
struct_fields.evidence: The complete set of +0x1090/+0x1094/+0x1098 sites in .text, from a chunked sweep of 2,755,661 instructions with resumes reaching 0xD2AFFE: ctor 0x4C99EB-0x4C99F7 (three dword zeros) and 0x4C9FEA-0x4CA037 (reserve, push_back 0 per ProductionDistribution); dtor 0x4CA9F9-0x4CAA18; LoadKey 0x4CE88E (0x4A8590 erase, 0x45F450 read); SaveContents 0x4D19AF (SaveWriteIntVector with ECX = 0x696, behind cmp [eax+4],[esi+0xCA8] at 0x4D19AA, eax from [esi+0xF1C]'s slot 23); CCountry_Reset 0x4D4796; BuildSliders 0x7FC557-0x7FC578; BalanceSliders 0x7FE1D1-0x7FE1F9; CTechnologyView::Build 0x81A649-0x81A666; unwind funclets 0xC24537, 0xC9C9FD. Savegame oracle: grep over 61 .hoi3 files in three save folders (the base game's 43, BlackICE 15.1's 7, BlackICE GitHub's 11) - one slider_locks in each of 60, inside the `player=` country's block (IRE at line 520305 of Ireland1938_08_03_14, GER in Germany1936_04_20_03), always six zeros. saveTokens.json: 1686 = slider_locks.

struct_fields.name: slider_locks_end
struct_fields.comment: One past the last of slider_locks. Both views bound their index by (this - +0x1090) / 4.
struct_fields.evidence: Zeroed with +0x1090 and +0x1098 in the constructor (0x4C99F1) and the destructor (0x4CAA12); read as the end at 0x7FC557, 0x7FE1D1, 0x81A649.

struct_fields.name: slider_locks_capacity
struct_fields.evidence: Written only by the constructor (0x4C99F7) and the destructor (0x4CAA18) as the third dword of the vector, the std::vector shape FINDINGS-factbase.md reads off the same initialiser. `confirmed` for the shape, the role from that shape.
